newsitem.title: USA: CNBC says BT planning to buy MCI.
newsitem.headline: CNBC says BT planning to buy MCI.

text.p: Television channel CNBC on Friday said that British Telecommunications Plc is in negotations to buy the remaining 80 percent of MCI Communications Corp it does not already own.
"MCI... is in negotiations to be bought by its 20 percent owner Britsh Telecom, and sources close to the deal tell me it could be announced as early as Monday morning," a CNBC reporter said.
Both companies, contacted by Reuters, had earlier declined to comment on the rumor, which had been circulating in the Nasdaq market.
CNBC said Lazard Freres, MCI's investment bankers, and Morgan Stanley were working on the deal, which it said could be worth upwards of $22 billion.
The reporter said that he had not been able to find out the price of the deal, but one analyst had estimated MCI would be worth $40 or so per share.

The Telecom Act of 1996 gives a reciprocity deal which would allow BT to increase its stake beyond the foreign ownership limit set under a 1934 Act if its home market was judged sufficiently open, the reporter said.
